newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO seen steady, swaps up marginally.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO seen steady, swaps up marginally.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil market was moving into a typical year-end lull as discussions remained thin and prices were expected to stay steady, traders said.
"Some firms have started to close their books and some traders are already taking their annual holidays," said a trader.
"Amid a quiet market, the market is unlikely to move by leaps and bounds," he said.
High sulphur, 180-centistoke grade fuel oil was quoted at $121/$123 per tonne on Wednesday, barely moved from Monday's quotes.
Traders said prices were likely to be steady on balanced demand and supply fundamentals. They said Chinese demand were keeping prices supported while regional supplies remained healthy.

Late Wednesday, a cargo of 180-centistoke fuel oil cargo for end-December lifting was offered at $125 per tonne, $2 per barrel higher from Tuesday's offers. It was offered late Wednesday at $124 fir December 26-30 lifting fob.
In the swaps market, December was up marginally, at $120.75/$121.75, 25 cents higher from Tuesday's quotes.
